summary: Alicia Haddick argues that Pokémon has evolved from a video game into an everyday lifestyle brand, using the Japanese live-action series PokéTsume as the prime example. She traces a roughly 15-year transformation from the 2006 sales slump and Pokémon Garden through anime diversification, charity and tourism efforts, merchandise for adults and infants, and Pokémon Go. The 2023 World Championships in Yokohama and record profits show the franchise now offers something for every age.
one_line: Pokémon's 15-year shift from kids' game to lifestyle brand is epitomized by the live-action series PokéTsume and the 2023 Yokohama World Championships.
key_facts: PokéTsume (Pack Your Pocket With Adventure, or Pocket ni Bouken o Tsumekonde) is the first Japanese live-action Pokémon TV series and premiered in Japan in October 2023 per the 'last month' reference.
The only prior live-action Pokémon storytelling was 2019's Detective Pikachu, starring Ryan Reynolds' wisecracking Pikachu.
PokéTsume follows Madoka Akagi, played by Nogizaka46 idol Nanase Nishino, a recent graduate who moves to the city to work at a startup called ADventure and rediscovers Pokémon Red and Blue.

The show parallels working life with the Pokémon journey: a rival is a childhood friend at another company, a product presentation is a gym battle, and on-the-job growth turns a Magikarp into a Gyarados.
In 2006, ahead of Pokémon Diamond and Pearl for Nintendo DS, sales had been declining, and the Hoenn GBA games were the worst-selling mainline titles.
Game Freak launched the Japan-only Pokémon Garden on the Yahoo! Kids portal, which had over 5 million unique monthly users; Diamond and Pearl then sold one-third more copies than Ruby and Sapphire.
Pokémon Origins was the first spinoff to bring in external studios, led by Production I.G and Xebec, after OLM had animated Pokémon since 1998.

Since then at least six web series have been made by outside partners, including this summer's Path to the Peak, set in the real world around the TCG, and the upcoming Netflix stop-motion series Pokémon Concierge.
In 2017 the annual Pokémon film series abandoned continuity with the TV anime, enabling CG experiments and Wit Studio's 2018 movie The Power of Us.
After the March 2011 Tohoku and Fukushima earthquake and tsunami, The Pokémon Company established the Pokémon With You Foundation, offering educational materials, food drives and scholarships.
Local government partnerships produced Yokohama's yearly Pikachu Outbreak and the Pokémon Local Acts initiative, which originated Japan's Pokémon-themed manhole covers.
Merchandise for older fans included monpoke, a line for infants, and the now-discontinued Pokémon Shirts of button-up shirts and workwear.
The 2023 Pokémon World Championships, the first held in Japan, took place in Yokohama with drone shows, pop-up Pokémon Centers, an orchestral concert and a cruise ship turned into the SS Anne.
Both new mainline Switch entries have sold over 20 million copies, and The Pokémon Company has recorded record profits and revenue in recent years.
